definition_zh: 倾向；趋势；癖性
definition_en: a leaning or inclination toward a particular kind of behaviour, direction or outcome
core_image: 一枚小球放在微微倾斜的桌面上，手一松，它总是往同一个方向滚
scene: 议事厅里，同一批人每次表决都往同一个方向靠，连反对者也渐渐跟着举手。There was a clear tendency for the committee to side with the older members.
sceneCN: 这里本词指群体在反复选择中表现出的固定偏向（第 1 个义项：一般倾向）；句意为委员会明显倾向于站在年长成员一边。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

senses.title: A general leaning
senses.definition: a general leaning of people or things toward one kind of behaviour or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物总体上偏向某一类行为或结果的态势
senses.example: There is a general tendency for prices to rise before holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 节前价格上涨存在一种普遍倾向。
senses.why: The word began as a stretched direction, and the first sense is that leaning seen in a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 本词最初指被拉伸的方向，第一个义项就是整个群体表现出的这种偏向。

senses.title: A personal habit of mind
senses.definition: a person's habitual inclination to act or feel in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在行为或感受上习惯性的偏向
senses.example: She has a tendency to interrupt when she is nervous.
senses.exampleCN: 她紧张时有打断别人的癖性。
senses.why: A single person also leans one way again and again, and the word names that private tilt.
senses.whyCN: 单个人也会一次次往同一侧倾，本词就指这种私人的偏向。

senses.title: A statistical movement
senses.definition: the direction in which a set of figures moves over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据在一段时间内变动的方向
senses.example: The figures show an upward tendency in household savings.
senses.exampleCN: 数据显示家庭储蓄呈上升趋势。
senses.why: Numbers plotted over time lean visibly, and that lean is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 按时间画出的数据会显出倾斜，本词描述的正是这种倾斜。

senses.title: A current of opinion
senses.definition: a broad drift of opinion or policy in a society at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期社会舆论或政策上广泛出现的走向
senses.example: A reformist tendency gained ground among younger voters.
senses.exampleCN: 改革倾向在年轻选民中占了上风。
senses.why: When many minds lean together, the lean becomes a public current rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的心思同时倾斜，这种倾斜就成了公共潮流而非私人情绪。

senses.title: A physical drift
senses.definition: the direction in which a body or substance naturally moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 物体或物质自然移动或变化的方向
senses.example: Hot air has a tendency to rise above cooler air.
senses.exampleCN: 热空气有升到冷空气之上的趋向。
senses.why: The oldest image is physical: something stretched or pulled toward a point.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是物理性的：某物被拉向某一点。

senses.title: A medical susceptibility
senses.definition: a bodily weakness that makes a person likely to develop a particular illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上的弱点使人容易患上某种疾病
senses.example: The condition runs in families with a tendency to low bone density.
senses.exampleCN: 该病多见于有骨密度偏低易感性的家族。
senses.why: A body leaning toward illness is described with the same word as any other lean.
senses.whyCN: 身体向疾病倾斜，用的仍是与其它倾斜相同的词。

senses.title: A stylistic leaning in art
senses.definition: a recurring preference for certain forms or moods in an artist's work
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家作品中反复出现的对某些形式或情绪的偏好
senses.example: His later novels show a tendency toward long, quiet scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 他后期的小说显出偏爱篇幅长而安静的场景。
senses.why: Style is a repeated lean of the hand, and critics borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 风格是手反复倾斜的结果，评论者便借用这个词来指它。

senses.title: A market drift
senses.definition: the direction in which prices or demand appear to be heading
senses.definitionCN: 价格或需求看起来正在走向的方向
senses.example: Traders watched the tendency of the index for the week.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员盯着这一周指数的走势。
senses.why: Markets are read as leaning one way, so forecasters speak of a tendency rather than a certainty.
senses.whyCN: 市场被看作正在往一侧倾，故预测者说倾向而不说定论。

intro.en: Tendency comes from the Latin verb for stretching or aiming, through a medieval Latin noun for a leaning; it is not related to the word for a trend, which comes from an Old English verb for turning.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，经中世纪拉丁语表「倾斜」的名词进入英语；它与表「走势」的那个词并不同源，后者出自古英语中表「转动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to stretch out, hold out or aim, and the image is a body or a line extended toward a point.
items.cn: 这一拉丁动词意为「伸出、朝向、瞄准」，意象是身体或线条朝某一点展开。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed a noun from the participle of that verb, naming a leaning or an inclination.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用该动词的分词造出名词，指倾斜或倾向。

items.en: English took the noun in the seventeenth century for a leaning of mind, body or fortune.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该名词，指心思、身体或运势上的偏向。

items.en: The word for a trend is not a relative: it comes from an Old English verb meaning to turn or revolve, and only later came to mean a direction.
items.cn: 表「走势」的那个词并非同族：它出自古英语中表「转动、旋转」的动词，后来才引申为方向。

items.en: Source uncertain: the older shape of the Latin verb is generally reconstructed, and the first English citation of the noun is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁动词的更早形态一般为重构，该名词在英语中的最早书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close to this noun; group two collects words for leanings of mind or body.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的形式；第二组是表示心思或身体偏向的词。

entries.definition: A true relative: the verb means to be inclined or to take care of, and the noun adds a suffix of state.
entries.definitionCN: 确为同源：动词表示趋向或照管，名词则加上表状态的后缀。

entries.definition: It means pushing a one-sided view, built on the same leaning root with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 意为推行片面观点，由同一表「倾斜」的词根加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Often treated as a synonym but a different word: it comes from an Old English verb for turning, not from the Latin verb for stretching, so the two are not cognate.
entries.definitionCN: 常被当作同义词，其实是另一个词：它出自古英语表「转动」的动词，而非拉丁语表「伸展」的动词，二者并无同源关系。

entries.definition: It sounds almost the same but comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold, and it names the right to occupy property rather than a leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，却出自拉丁语表「握持」的动词，指占用房产的权利，与偏向无关。

entries.definition: A leaning of mind or body, closer to a settled preference than to a measured direction in figures.
entries.definitionCN: 心思或身体上的倾斜，更接近固定的偏好，而非数据中被测量的方向。

entries.definition: A strong natural tendency to behave in a particular way, usually toward something undesirable.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈而天生的行为偏向，通常指向不受欢迎的事。

entries.definition: A person's habitual temperament, the whole cast of mind rather than one lean.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人习惯的性情，是整个心性而非单一偏向。

entries.definition: A slow general movement or change of opinion, stressing gradual motion rather than a built-in lean.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的整体移动或舆论变化，强调渐进，而非内在的倾斜。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to stretch: a line pulled toward a point, and that is the image of the whole family.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为伸展：一条被拉向某点的线，这就是整个词族的意象。

normal.en: The family runs tendency, tend, tendentious, tendentiously, tendentiousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括倾向、趋向、有偏向的、带有偏向地与偏向性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a tendency to overreact, a downward tendency, a growing tendency.
normal.cn: 固定说法：过度反应的倾向、下降趋势、日益增长的趋势。

normal.en: Keep it apart from the word for a trend: that one came from an old verb for turning, not from stretching.
normal.cn: 要与表「走势」的那个词分开：后者出自表「转动」的古动词，并非出自「伸展」。

normal.en: Statistics speak of a tendency when a line on a chart slants; medicine speaks of one when a body is likely to fall ill.
normal.cn: 统计学说倾向，是指图表上的线出现斜度；医学说倾向，是指身体容易生病。

abstract.en: Picture a metal ball rolling toward the low edge of a tilted table, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗金属球一次次滚向倾斜桌面的低边。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one side of a square without anyone giving an order.
abstract.cn: 想象人群没有接到任何指令，却慢慢移向广场的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that always reaches for the same pen, even when another lies closer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手总去拿同一支笔，哪怕另一支离得更近。

examples.en: Prices show a tendency to fall after the harvest.
examples.cn: 收成之后价格显出下跌的倾向。

examples.en: He has a tendency to talk over people in meetings.
examples.cn: 他在会上有抢别人话头的癖性。

examples.en: The survey found a tendency toward smaller households.
examples.cn: 调查发现家庭规模有变小的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「伸展」记成一条被拉向某处的线：线往哪边斜，就是往哪边倾向。

root: 来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，中世纪拉丁语由其分词构成表「倾斜」的名词，英语借入后指各种偏向；与表「走势」的词不同源，后者出自古英语表「转动」的动词；更深来源一般为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: a line or a body stretched toward one point, so that it leans the same way each time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：一条线或一具身体被拉向某一点，于是每次都往同一侧倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a tilted table, always rolling to the same low corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾斜桌面上的球，总滚向同一个低角。

branches.en: LEANING LINE: the general lean of people and the physical drift of matter share one image of a stretched line.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线：人群的整体偏向与物质的物理趋向共享「被拉长的线」这一意象。

branches.en: PRIVATE LEAN: one person's repeated tilt becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 私人偏向：一个人反复的倾斜成为心理习性。

branches.en: MEASURED SLANT: charts and markets are read as leaning, so the word names a direction in figures.
branches.cn: 可测的斜度：图表与市场都被读作倾斜，本词于是指数据中的方向。

branches.en: PUBLIC CURRENT: many minds leaning together become a drift of opinion.
branches.cn: 公共潮流：许多心思同时倾斜，便成舆论走向。

branches.en: BODY AND ART: a body likely to fall ill and a hand that prefers certain forms both lean in the same old sense.
branches.cn: 身体与艺术：易患病的身体与偏爱某些形式的手，都在同一古老意义上倾斜。

intro.en: The noun is built from a Latin verb and a suffix of state, and English keeps a small family around it, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语动词加表状态的后缀构成，英语周围还保留少量同族词，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb supplies the stretching, the Latin participle supplies the leaning, and English supplies only the closing noun suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词提供「伸展」，拉丁语分词提供「倾斜」，英语只提供收尾的名词后缀。

items.example: The root shows in extend, intend and tension, all about stretching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于延伸、打算、张力等词，都与伸展有关。

items.example: A bowstring is stretched, and so is a plan toward its aim.
items.exampleCN: 弓弦被拉紧，计划也朝目标伸展。

items.example: The participle describes what is already leaning.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词描述已经在倾斜的东西。

items.structure: tendens plus a medieval Latin noun suffix
items.example: The medieval noun turned the act of leaning into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪名词把倾斜这一动作变成一种事物。

items.meaning: a leaning toward a kind of act or outcome
items.example: A tendency can be measured over many cases.
items.exampleCN: 倾向可以在许多个案上被测量出来。

items.example: The report was tendentious from its first line.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告从第一行起就带有偏向。

items.meaning: the quality of pushing a lean
items.example: Readers objected to the tendentiousness of the piece.
items.exampleCN: 读者反对这篇文章的偏向性。

items.structure: Latin prefix plus the root tend-
items.example: They extended the deadline by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把截止期限延长了一周。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch, to extend, to aim

由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」

definition_zh: 温柔的；嫩的；疼痛的；正式提出；投标；照管者
definition_en: gentle and careful; easily painful; or to offer something formally; also a formal offer or a caregiver
core_image: 碰一下就皱眉的嫩芽，也是递出标书时轻放的手
scene: 照看幼苗的人连浇水都放轻了手。The young plants need tender care in the first weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 tender 是形容词「精心呵护的、温柔的」（第 1 个义项：温柔体贴的）；句意：幼苗头几周需要温柔细致的照料。

derivatives.zh: 温柔地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
温柔；触痛（形容词加 -ness 构成）
使肉变嫩（形容词加 -ize 动词后缀）

senses.title: Gentle, loving and careful
senses.definition: showing gentleness, kindness and care
senses.definitionCN: 表现出温柔、善意与呵护
senses.example: She gave the rescued kitten tender care.
senses.exampleCN: 她悉心照料获救的小猫。
senses.why: The image is the young shoot: what is soft needs and receives a soft touch.
senses.whyCN: 意象是嫩芽：柔弱之物需要也召来轻柔的触碰。

senses.title: Soft and easy to cut or chew
senses.definition: soft and easy to bite, used of meat or plants
senses.definitionCN: 柔软易咬的，用于肉或植物
senses.example: Slow cooking makes the beef tender.
senses.exampleCN: 慢炖使牛肉软嫩。
senses.why: Physical softness is the literal shoot image: tender flesh yields to the touch.
senses.whyCN: 物理的柔嫩是「嫩芽」意象的直取：嫩肉一按即让。

senses.title: Painful when touched
senses.definition: sensitive or painful to touch, used of skin or muscles
senses.definitionCN: 触碰即痛，用于皮肤或肌肉
senses.example: The bruise is still tender.
senses.exampleCN: 淤伤一按还疼。
senses.why: The shoot also flinches: what is soft hurts when pressed.
senses.whyCN: 嫩芽也会躲闪：柔弱之处一经按压便喊疼。

senses.title: To offer something formally
senses.definition: to present something officially, such as a resignation or a bid
senses.definitionCN: 正式呈递某物，如辞呈或标书
senses.example: He tendered his resignation this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他今早正式递交辞呈。
senses.why: A formal offer is handled with both hands, gently placed: the same soft touch, now ceremonial.
senses.whyCN: 正式呈递之物以双手轻放：同一种轻柔触碰，只是此番带上仪式感。

senses.title: A formal offer or bid
senses.definition: a written offer to do work or supply goods at a fixed price
senses.definitionCN: 按定价承接工程或供货的书面报价
senses.example: Five companies submitted tenders for the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 五家公司提交了大桥工程投标。
senses.why: The offer itself is named by the gesture: the placed document is a tender.
senses.whyCN: 报价以那个动作命名：被轻轻放上桌的文件，就叫 tender。

senses.title: A person or boat that attends another
senses.titleCN: 照管者；随侍人员；补给船
senses.definition: a person or small boat that serves or attends to a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 照看他人或为主船服务的小船或人员
senses.example: The bar tender kept everyone's glasses full.
senses.exampleCN: 酒吧侍者让大家的杯子一直满着。
senses.why: The one who tends is named after the care itself: attendance is tenderness in work clothes.
senses.whyCN: 照管者以「照料」为名：随侍就是穿上工装的温柔。

intro.en: English has two tenders. The soft one comes from Latin tener, delicate, through Old French tendre. The offer one comes from tendere, to stretch toward, the same root as tend.
intro.cn: 英语有两个 tender。「柔嫩」的 tender 出自拉丁语 tener「柔嫩」，经古法语 tendre 传入；「提出、投标」的 tender 出自 tendere「朝…伸去」，与 tend 同根。

items.en: Tener meant delicate, soft, young; its deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: tener 意为柔嫩、幼小；其更深词根不确定。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch toward, and its participle tensus gives tense.
items.cn: tendere 意为朝某方向拉伸，分词 tensus 生成 tense。

items.en: Old French tendre carried both Latin words, soft and stretching, into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tendre 把拉丁两词——柔嫩与拉伸——一并带入英语。

items.en: English borrowed tendre twice: the soft adjective and the offer verb.
items.cn: 英语两度借入 tendre：柔嫩的形容词与呈递的动词。

items.en: Commerce fixed the bid sense, medicine kept the pain sense, and cooking kept the meat sense.
items.cn: 商业固定投标义，医学保留触痛义，烹饪保留嫩肉义。

note.en: The two tenders are distinguished from each other and set beside softness words.
note.cn: 区分两个 tender，并将其与表示柔软的词并列。

entries.definition: to incline or care for; shares the stretch root with the offer tender
entries.definitionCN: 倾向；照料；与「提出」义的 tender 同根

entries.definition: in a gentle way
entries.definitionCN: 温柔地

entries.definition: the cord that stretches muscle to bone
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱；连接肌肉与骨骼的拉紧之索

entries.definition: mild and kind in manner
entries.definitionCN: 温和的；和善的

entries.definition: not hard or firm
entries.definitionCN: 软的；不坚硬的

entries.definition: a formal offer of a price
entries.definitionCN: 出价；投标（对照词）

normalIntro.en: Real links: tener soft, tendere stretch, the bid on the table, and tender age.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tener「柔嫩」、tendere「拉伸」、桌上的标书、tender age。

normal.en: Tener means delicate: a tender leaf bends before it breaks.
normal.cn: tener 意为柔嫩：嫩叶先弯后折。

normal.en: Tendere means stretch toward: you tender a document by stretching out your hand.
normal.cn: tendere 意为朝…伸去：tender 文件就是把手伸出去。

normal.en: Tender meat has yielded to slow fire.
normal.cn: 嫩肉是向文火投降的肉。

normal.en: Tender age: the soft years that flinch at every touch.
normal.cn: tender age：一碰就缩的柔弱年岁。

normal.en: A bid called a tender is placed, not thrown.
normal.cn: 被称为 tender 的标书是「轻放」而非「抛出」的。

abstract.en: Softness is strength that has agreed to be careful.
abstract.cn: 柔是同意小心行事的力。

abstract.en: The hand that gives is the same hand that soothes.
abstract.cn: 给予的手与安抚的手是同一只手。

abstract.en: What flinches teaches the world to touch slowly.
abstract.cn: 会缩的东西教会世界放慢触碰。

examples.en: The nurse handled the wound with tender hands.
examples.cn: 护士用温柔的手处理伤口。

examples.en: The company tendered for the new tunnel project.
examples.cn: 该公司投标了新隧道工程。

examples.en: Steamed fish should be tender, not tough.
examples.cn: 蒸鱼应当软嫩，不能老韧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「疼得」——伤口疼得一碰就缩，得轻点碰 → tender 触痛的、温柔的

root: 两个来源：「柔嫩」义出自拉丁语 tener「嫩的」（经古法语 tendre）；「提出、投标、照管」义出自拉丁语 tendere「朝…伸去」（ad- + tendere 的 attend/tend 一族）。

sensesIntro.en: Two histories meet in one spelling: the shoot that bends, and the hand stretched out with an offer.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种历史共用一个拼写：会弯的嫩芽，与递出报价时伸出的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young shoot, and an outstretched hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株嫩芽，与一只伸出的手。

branches.en: Softness of manner and of meat share one leaf.
branches.cn: 态度之柔与肉质之嫩共用一片嫩叶。

branches.en: The shoot flinches when pressed.
branches.cn: 嫩芽被按便闪躲。

branches.en: The stretched hand presents the bid.
branches.cn: 伸出的手呈递标书。

branches.en: The tender of a ship attends the large one.
branches.cn: 补给船随侍大船。

branches.en: Care is softness given a job.
branches.cn: 照料是被派了任务的柔软。

intro.en: Tender stands between two Latin roots: tener, soft, and tendere, stretch.
intro.cn: tender 处于两个拉丁词根之间：tener「柔嫩」与 tendere「拉伸」。

latinIntro.en: Latin tener means delicate; Latin tendere means to stretch toward; both reached English through Old French tendre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tener 意为柔嫩；tendere 意为朝…伸去；两者经古法语 tendre 进入英语。

definition_zh: 紧张的；绷紧的；（动词的）时态；使紧张
definition_en: tightly stretched or nervous; also the form of a verb showing time
core_image: 一根被拉到极限的琴弦
scene: 考试铃响前，教室里安静得能听见笔尖。Everyone went tense as the results were announced.
sceneCN: 这里 tense 是形容词「紧张的」（第 1 个义项：精神紧绷）；句意：成绩宣布时所有人都紧张起来。

derivatives.zh: 张力；紧张（分词 tensus 加 -ion 构成）
紧张地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
肌腱（同根名词，被拉紧的索）

senses.title: Nervous and unable to relax
senses.definition: feeling worried and unable to relax
senses.definitionCN: 焦虑不安、无法放松的
senses.example: She felt tense before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她很紧张。
senses.why: The string image: a mind pulled tight like a cord ready to snap.
senses.whyCN: 琴弦意象：心被拉得像一根随时会断的弦。

senses.title: Tightly stretched
senses.definition: stretched tight, used of muscles, ropes or wires
senses.definitionCN: 被拉紧的，用于肌肉、绳索或钢丝
senses.example: Climb with tense arms and steady legs.
senses.exampleCN: 攀岩时手臂绷紧、双腿站稳。
senses.why: This is the literal root sense: the cord pulled to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面义：绳索被拉到极限。

senses.title: A verb form showing time
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows when an action happens
senses.definitionCN: 表明动作发生时间的动词形式
senses.example: English uses the past tense for finished actions.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用过去时表示已完成动作。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the stretched string for time stretched along a line.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了绷紧的弦，来比喻沿时间线拉开的动作。

senses.title: To make a muscle or person tight
senses.definition: to tighten a muscle or make someone anxious
senses.definitionCN: 使肌肉收紧或使人心绪紧张
senses.example: He tensed his shoulders before lifting.
senses.exampleCN: 举重前他绷紧了双肩。
senses.why: The adjective turns into an action: pulling the string on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为动作：主动去拉那根弦。

intro.en: Tense, tight, comes from Latin tendere, to stretch, through its participle tensus. The grammar tense is a separate borrowing of Latin tempus, time.
intro.cn: 「紧绷」的 tense 源自拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」的分词 tensus；语法「时态」的 tense 则另借拉丁语 tempus「时间」。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch; tensus meant stretched tight.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸；tensus 意为绷紧的。

items.en: Tendere is usually traced to a reconstructed PIE root for stretching.
items.cn: tendere 一般被追溯到重构的印欧「拉伸」词根。

items.en: Old French tens passed the tight sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tens 把「绷紧」义传入英语。

items.en: The grammar term entered separately from Old French temps, Latin tempus.
items.cn: 语法术语经古法语 temps（拉丁 tempus）另行进入。

items.en: Spelling merged both words as tense; context tells the time-word from the tight-word.
items.cn: 两词拼合为 tense；语境区分「时间」与「紧绷」。

note.en: Tense is compared with its stretch family and with nerves words.
note.cn: 把 tense 与「拉伸」词族及表示神经紧绷的词对比。

entries.definition: the state of being stretched or strained
entries.definitionCN: 张力；紧张

entries.definition: the cord joining muscle and bone
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱

entries.definition: a stretched cloth shelter
entries.definitionCN: 帐篷；同一拉伸词根的另一产物

entries.definition: worried and frightened about something
entries.definitionCN: 紧张的；不安的

entries.definition: pulled tight, no slack
entries.definitionCN: 拉紧的；不松垮的

entries.definition: pressure or tension on body or mind
entries.definitionCN: 压力；劳损

normalIntro.en: Real links: tensus stretched, the tense-tension-tendon family, and the time word hidden in grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tensus「绷紧」、tense/tension/tendon 词族、藏在语法里的时间词。

normal.en: Tensus means stretched: a tense rope hums when plucked.
normal.cn: tensus 意为绷紧：紧绷的绳一拨就嗡嗡响。

normal.en: Tense up before the dive: pull every string in the body.
normal.cn: 跳水前 tense up：把全身的弦都拉紧。

normal.en: Grammar tense is tempus, time wearing a verb's coat.
normal.cn: 语法 tense 就是 tempus：时间穿着动词的外衣。

normal.en: Tension in the room: everyone is a drawn bow.
normal.cn: 屋里的 tension：人人都像拉满的弓。

normal.en: A tendon is a living rope, always a little tense.
normal.cn: 肌腱是活的绳，永远微微绷着。

abstract.en: A nerve and a wire behave the same when pulled.
abstract.cn: 神经与钢丝被拉紧时表现相同。

abstract.en: Time itself is a string grammar likes to stretch.
abstract.cn: 时间本身就是一根语法爱拉紧的弦。

abstract.en: Relaxation is simply letting the string slack.
abstract.cn: 放松不过是让弦松下来。

examples.en: The room went tense when the verdict was read.
examples.cn: 宣判时屋里气氛骤然紧张。

examples.en: Past tense verbs often end in ed.
examples.cn: 过去式动词常以 ed 结尾。

examples.en: Relax your tense shoulders and breathe.
examples.cn: 放松紧绷的肩膀，深呼吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摊死」——紧张得像摊开又拉死的弦，一动就断 → tense 紧张的、时态

root: 「紧绷」义：拉丁 tendere「拉伸」分词 tensus → 古法语 tens → 英语 tense；「时态」义另借拉丁 tempus「时间」（经古法语 temps），两词拼写合流。

sensesIntro.en: One spelling, two strings: the pulled cord and the stretched line of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拼写，两根弦：被拉紧的绳与被拉开的时间线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string pulled to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉到极限的弦。

branches.en: The literal cord, humming.
branches.cn: 字面之弦，嗡嗡作响。

branches.en: The body and the room both tighten.
branches.cn: 身体与房间都会收紧。

branches.en: Grammar keeps time on a line.
branches.cn: 语法把时间排在一条线上。

branches.en: A drawn bow is a waiting sentence.
branches.cn: 拉满的弓是一句等待中的判词。

branches.en: Release is the other half of tense.
branches.cn: 「松开」是 tense 的另一半。

intro.en: Tense shares the tendere stretch family with tension, tendon and tent.
intro.cn: tense 与 tension、tendon、tent 同属 tendere「拉伸」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, to stretch, has the participle tensus, source of the tight sense; the grammar tense is from tempus, time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」分词 tensus 是「紧绷」义之源；语法义出自 tempus「时间」。

definition_zh: 拉力；张力；紧张；紧张关系；电压；表面张力
definition_en: the state of being stretched tight, the pulling force in something stretched, or a state of nervous strain between people
core_image: 拔河绳被两队拉得笔直，中间的红布几乎不动，绳子发出细微的吱响
scene: 拔河绳被两队拉得笔直，中间的红布几乎不动，绳子发出细微的吱响。The tension in the rope rises until it begins to creak.
sceneCN: 这里指绷紧的绳索内部承受的拉力（第 1 个义项：拉力、张力）；句意为绳中的拉力不断上升，直到绳子开始吱响。图中可辨识物件：拔河绳、红布标记、两队队员、地面标线。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干经法语而来，义为「紧张的；拉紧」
由该名词加表示「可……的」的形容词尾构成，义为「可拉伸的」
由该名词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「紧张度」
由表示「过度」的前缀加该名词构成，义为「高血压」
由该名词加表示关系的形容词尾构成，义为「张力的」

senses.title: The pull in a stretched object
senses.definition: the pulling force carried by a rope, cable or rod that is stretched between two points
senses.definitionCN: 被拉在两点之间的绳、缆或杆所承受的拉力
senses.example: The tension in the cable holds the mast upright.
senses.exampleCN: 缆索中的拉力使桅杆保持直立。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stretch, and the noun names the force that stretching produces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为拉伸，这个名词指拉伸所产生的力。

senses.title: Strain between people
senses.titleCN: 人与人之间的紧张关系
senses.definition: a state of distrust or hostility between people, groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 人、群体或国家之间不信任或敌对的状态
senses.example: Tension between the two teams slowed the work.
senses.exampleCN: 两队之间的紧张关系拖慢了工作。
senses.why: A stretched rope is ready to snap, and relationships under pressure are described by the same image.
senses.whyCN: 拉紧的绳随时会断，承受压力的关系被同一个画面描述。

senses.title: Nervous strain
senses.definition: a feeling of worry and readiness that makes the body or mind tight
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或心智绷紧的担忧与戒备感
senses.example: The waiting room was full of tension before the result.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来前，候诊室里满是紧张。
senses.why: The body tenses like a rope, and the physical word became the standard term for anxiety.
senses.whyCN: 身体像绳子一样绷紧，这个物理词成了焦虑的标准说法。

senses.title: Electrical potential
senses.definition: the electrical potential difference between two points, especially in older European usage
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间的电势差，尤见于较早的欧洲用法
senses.example: The sign warned of high tension in the line.
senses.exampleCN: 标牌警告线路带有高压。
senses.why: Early electrical science pictured voltage as a stretched state, and several European languages still say tension.
senses.whyCN: 早期电学把电压想象成一种绷紧状态，若干欧洲语言至今仍用「张力」一词。

senses.title: The skin of a liquid
senses.definition: the force at the surface of a liquid that makes it behave like a thin elastic sheet
senses.definitionCN: 液体表面使自身表现得像一层薄弹性膜的力量
senses.example: Surface tension keeps the droplet round.
senses.exampleCN: 表面张力使液滴保持圆形。
senses.why: Molecules at the surface pull on each other like a stretched membrane, so the old word fits exactly.
senses.whyCN: 表面分子彼此拉扯，像一张绷紧的膜，老词用得恰到好处。

senses.title: The tightness of a setting
senses.definition: the degree to which something is pulled tight, as in a belt or a string
senses.definitionCN: 某物被拉紧的程度，如皮带或琴弦
senses.example: Adjust the tension until the belt deflects ten millimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 调整张紧度，直到皮带下垂十毫米。
senses.why: Tightness is a matter of degree, and maintenance work needs a word for that degree.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧是程度问题，维修工作需要一个词来表示这个程度。

senses.title: Dramatic suspense
senses.definition: the quality in a story or performance that keeps an audience waiting for what comes next
senses.definitionCN: 故事或表演中让观众等待后续的品质
senses.example: The film builds tension without showing the threat.
senses.exampleCN: 影片不露威胁，却把张力堆起来。
senses.why: An audience is held like a rope between two pulls, and the metaphor became a craft term.
senses.whyCN: 观众像被两股力量拉住的绳，这个比喻成了一门手艺术语。

senses.title: Muscular tightness
senses.definition: the involuntary tightness of muscles caused by stress or effort
senses.definitionCN: 因压力或用力而造成的肌肉不自主紧绷
senses.example: Massage reduced the tension in his shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 按摩缓解了他肩部的紧张。
senses.why: Muscle fibres literally shorten and tighten, and the word describes that state before it describes the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 肌纤维确实会缩短绷紧，这个词先描述这种状态，再描述那种感受。

intro.en: Tension comes from Latin tensio, a stretching, from tensus, the past participle of tendere, to stretch. French carried the noun into English, and the figurative senses followed the physical one.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 tensio「拉伸」，源自 tendere「拉伸」的过去分词 tensus。法语把名词带入英语，比喻义在物理义之后出现。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or extend, and it also stands behind English tend and tense.
items.cn: 这个词意为拉伸、伸展，也是英语 tend 与 tense 的来源。

items.en: The past participle meant stretched or extended, and it gave the adjective tense its tight sense.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为被拉伸、被伸展，给了形容词 tense「绷紧」的意思。

items.en: The noun named the act of stretching and the state of being stretched, with no separate word for the force.
items.cn: 这个名词指拉伸动作与被拉伸的状态，当时并没有单独的词表示拉力。

items.en: French tension reached English in the sixteenth century, first as a physical term and soon after as a mental one.
items.cn: 法语 tension 在十六世纪进入英语，先是物理术语，不久便用于心理。

items.en: The nineteenth century applied the word to voltage in several European languages, and which language coined that usage is source uncertain.
items.cn: 十九世纪若干欧洲语言把这个词用于电压；它最早出自哪种语言尚无定论，这一用法来源不确定。

items.en: Literary criticism borrowed the word for suspense, and physics kept it for surface and structural forces.
items.cn: 文学批评借这个词指悬念，物理学则保留它指表面与结构中的力。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like tension; the second group names neighbouring ideas of pulling and strain.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「tension」相近；第二组是与「拉伸、压力」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Tight or nervous, or a verb form that places an action in time.
entries.definitionCN: 指绷紧或紧张的，也指表示时间的动词形式。

entries.definition: Capable of being stretched without breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被拉伸而不断裂的。

entries.definition: Relating to tension, especially in geology or mechanics.
entries.definitionCN: 指与张力有关的，尤用于地质或力学。

entries.definition: A stretching out or an added part; it shares the Latin stretching verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指伸出或增加的部分；共享拉丁语「拉伸」动词。

entries.definition: Done without confidence; it looks close but comes from the word for trying.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有把握地做的；形近，但来自表示「尝试」的词。

entries.definition: Deformation under force, or pressure on body and mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指受力形变，或身心所受的压力。

entries.definition: Force per unit area inside a material, or mental pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指材料内部单位面积上的力，或精神压力。

entries.definition: Force applied over an area, or a demanding influence.
entries.definitionCN: 指施加在面积上的力，或一种施压的影响。

entries.definition: The feeling of waiting for an outcome that is not yet known.
entries.definitionCN: 指等待未知结果时的感受。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stretching verb, the real physics family and real engineering phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「拉伸」动词、真实物理同族词与真实工程搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to stretch, so tension is the state of being stretched.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为拉伸，所以 tension 就是被拉伸的状态。

normal.en: Tend, tense and tension all come from the same stretching stem.
normal.cn: tend、tense 与 tension 都出自同一个「拉伸」词干。

normal.en: Surface tension and high tension are the two technical phrases.
normal.cn: 表面张力与高压是两个技术说法。

normal.en: Under tension and ease the tension cover the physical and the social.
normal.cn: 受拉与缓解紧张分别覆盖物理与社会两个层面。

normal.en: Tensile strength is what decides whether a rope survives its tension.
normal.cn: 抗拉强度决定一根绳能不能撑住它的拉力。

abstract.en: Tension is force that has not yet been released.
abstract.cn: 张力是还没有释放的力。

abstract.en: A room can be as tight as a rope without anyone touching it.
abstract.cn: 一个房间可以像绳子一样绷紧，却没人碰它。

abstract.en: Suspense is tension with a clock attached.
abstract.cn: 悬念就是挂上时钟的张力。

examples.en: The tension in the tie rod was set with a gauge.
examples.cn: 拉杆的拉力用仪表设定。

examples.en: Tension grew as the deadline approached.
examples.cn: 期限临近，紧张气氛加重。

examples.en: A drop of soap lowers the surface tension of water.
examples.cn: 一滴肥皂液降低了水的表面张力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「藤申」——藤条被两头拉得直直的，一「申」手还能感到那股力：张力

root: 拉丁语 tensio「拉伸」← tensus（tendere「拉伸、伸展」的过去分词）；法语 tension 于十六世纪带入英语。比喻的「紧张」义随物理义而发展，十九世纪若干欧洲语言用它表示电压。同族有 tend、tense、tensile；各比喻用法定型的确切年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe something pulled: a cable, a relationship, a nervous body, a voltage, a liquid surface, a belt setting, an audience and a muscle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述被拉住的东西：缆索、关系、紧张的身体、电压、液面、皮带张紧度、观众与肌肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two teams pull one rope until the rope is straight and humming.
core.cn: 核心意象：两队人拉同一根绳，直到绳子笔直并发响。

branches.en: THE PULL AND ITS DEGREE: the force in a cable and the tightness a mechanic sets.
branches.cn: 拉力及其程度：缆索里的力，以及维修工设定的张紧度。

branches.en: THE TAUT RELATIONSHIP: distrust between groups and anxiety in a waiting room.
branches.cn: 绷紧的关系：群体间的猜疑，以及候诊室里的焦虑。

branches.en: THE ELECTRICAL STRETCH: potential waiting to discharge through a line.
branches.cn: 电的绷紧：等待沿线路释放的电势差。

branches.en: THE LIQUID SKIN: surface molecules pulling the drop into a round shape.
branches.cn: 液体的表皮：表面分子把液滴拉成圆形。

branches.en: THE HELD BODY: an audience waiting, and shoulders tightened by stress.
branches.cn: 被拉住的身体：等待的观众，以及因压力绷紧的肩膀。

intro.en: Tension is a Latin noun of stretching, carried by French, with a family that still produces physics and medical terms.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「拉伸」的拉丁名词，经法语传入，其词族至今仍在生成物理与医学术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, tensus and tensio are the real chain; the deeper root is reconstructed rather than recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 tendere、tensus 与 tensio 构成真实的链条；更深词根属重构，而非有记录形式。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的来源。

items.example: The noun is the direct source of tension.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 tension 的直接来源。

items.example: The ending carries the Latin noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把拉丁名词带入英语。

items.example: It builds tensile, able to be stretched.

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干经法语而来，义为「紧张的；拉紧」
由该名词加表示「可……的」的形容词尾构成，义为「可拉伸的」
由该名词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「紧张度」
由该名词加表示关系的形容词尾构成，义为「张力的」
由表示「过度」的前缀加该名词构成，义为「高血压」

definition_zh: 帐篷；帐蓬；（医疗）扩张探条
definition_en: a shelter made of cloth supported by poles and ropes
core_image: 一根中杆把一块大布顶成小屋
scene: 山谷营地中央，一块防水布被绳索绷成尖顶小屋。They pitched a tent beside the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 tent 是「帐篷」（第 1 个义项：布制临时居所）；句意：他们在湖边搭起帐篷。

pos.zh: 以帐篷遮盖；（古）用探条扩张

derivatives.zh: 帐篷设备；宿营装备（tent 加名词后缀 -age）
张布架（同根旧词，拉紧织物的架子）

senses.title: A cloth shelter
senses.definition: a portable shelter of cloth stretched over poles
senses.definitionCN: 用杆子撑起布面的便携居所
senses.example: The wind flattened their tent overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间风吹塌了他们的帐篷。
senses.why: The word keeps the idea of stretching: cloth is stretched over a frame to make a home.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留「张紧」之意：布被绷在骨架上，便成了居所。

senses.title: To camp in or cover with tents
senses.definition: to lodge in tents or to cover something like a tent
senses.definitionCN: 宿于帐篷，或像帐篷般覆盖
senses.example: The climbers tented below the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在山脊下扎营过夜。
senses.why: The shelter becomes an action: to tent is to make the stretched cloth happen.
senses.whyCN: 居所变成动作：to tent 就是把「张布为顶」这件事做出来。

senses.title: A surgical probe (old use)
senses.definition: in old medicine, a roll of soft material used to keep a wound open
senses.definitionCN: 旧医学中用以保持伤口张开的软质圆条
senses.example: Old surgical texts describe a wax tent for the wound.
senses.exampleCN: 旧外科文献描述用蜡制探条撑开伤口。
senses.why: The probe stretches tissue open just as canvas is stretched on poles, so the word migrated.
senses.whyCN: 探条把组织撑开，正如帆布被绷在杆上，词义因此迁移。

intro.en: Tent comes from Latin tendere, to stretch, through Old French tente, a stretched cloth shelter.
intro.cn: tent 源自拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」，经古法语 tente（张紧的布棚）进入英语。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or extend.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸、延展。

items.en: Tendere itself is usually traced to a PIE root for stretching, though the deeper form is reconstructed.
items.cn: tendere 一般被追溯到印欧语「拉伸」词根，深层形式系重构。

items.en: Old French tente named a stretched canvas shelter.
items.cn: 古法语 tente 指张紧的帆布棚。

items.en: English took tent for the shelter and kept the stretching idea.
items.cn: 英语借入 tent 指帐篷，并保留「拉伸」观念。

items.en: Camping made the noun common, and the old surgical sense survived in textbooks.
items.cn: 露营使名词义普及，旧外科义留存在教科书中。

note.en: Tent is compared with its stretching relatives and with other temporary shelters.
note.cn: 将 tent 与「拉伸」同族词及其他临时居所对比。

entries.definition: gentle, or to offer formally; shares the stretch root but is a separate word
entries.definitionCN: 温柔的；正式提出；同「拉伸」词根但属另一词

entries.definition: tightly stretched
entries.definitionCN: 绷紧的

entries.definition: a stretching organ of an octopus
entries.definitionCN: 触手；会伸展的器官

entries.definition: a cloth cover held above
entries.definitionCN: 顶篷；天幕

entries.definition: a place giving protection
entries.definitionCN: 庇护所

entries.definition: a temporary camp without tents
entries.definitionCN: 露营地；不设帐篷的临时宿营

normalIntro.en: Real links: tendere stretch, the tense-tentacle family, pitching and striking camp.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tendere「拉伸」、tense/tentacle 词族、搭营与拔营。

normal.en: Tent is cloth stretched over poles, from tendere.
normal.cn: tent 是绷在杆上的布，出自 tendere。

normal.en: Pitch a tent: stretch it out and pin it down.
normal.cn: pitch a tent：先拉张，再钉牢。

normal.en: Tense rope and tent cloth are the same pulling.
normal.cn: 绷紧的绳与帐篷布是同一种拉力。

normal.en: An octopus tentacle stretches like tent cloth.
normal.cn: 章鱼触手的伸展如帐篷布。

normal.en: Take down the tent: let the cloth fall slack.
normal.cn: 收帐篷：让布松下来。

abstract.en: A tent is a roof that agrees to be carried.
abstract.cn: 帐篷是同意被扛着走的屋顶。

abstract.en: Stretching is the shortest road between cloth and home.
abstract.cn: 「拉伸」是布与家之间最短的路。

abstract.en: Every camp is a sentence that ends at dawn.
abstract.cn: 每座营地都是一句在黎明结束的话。

examples.en: We shared one tent between four hikers.
examples.cn: 四名徒步者共用一顶帐篷。

examples.en: The scouts tented on the far bank of the river.
examples.cn: 童子军在河对岸扎营。

examples.en: A big white tent covered the wedding tables.
examples.cn: 一顶白色大帐篷罩住婚宴桌席。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「疼特」——露营夜里杆子倒了砸得头特别疼，帐篷记一生 → tent 帐篷

root: 拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」→ 通俗拉丁语 tenta「张紧之物」→ 古法语 tente「布棚」→ 英语 tent「帐篷」；与 tense、tender、tentacle 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From stretched canvas come the shelter, the camping verb, and the old wound probe.
sensesIntro.cn: 从绷紧的帆布长出居所、露营动词与旧时的伤口探条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth pulled taut into a room.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉紧成房间的布。

branches.en: The stretched cloth is the house.
branches.cn: 绷紧的布即屋。

branches.en: To tent is to perform the stretch nightly.
branches.cn: to tent 就是每晚重演这次拉伸。

branches.en: A wax roll stretches tissue as poles stretch canvas.
branches.cn: 蜡条撑开组织，如杆撑开帆布。

branches.en: Camping turns nouns into nights.
branches.cn: 露营把名词变成夜晚。

branches.en: Wind tests every taut surface.
branches.cn: 风考验每张绷紧的表面。

intro.en: Tent shares the tendere stretch family with tense, tender and tentacle.
intro.cn: tent 与 tense、tender、tentacle 同属 tendere「拉伸」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, to stretch, produced tensus and the family of tension words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」产生分词 tensus 与 tension 一族。

definition_zh: 第十；十分之一
definition_en: coming after nine others in order, or one part of ten equal parts
core_image: 十根手指里最后立起的那一根
scene: 跑道尽头标着十个刻度，最后那条线属于领先者。He finished the race in tenth place.
sceneCN: 这里 tenth 是「第十」（第 1 个义项：序数）；句意：他赛跑得了第十名。

derivatives.zh: 第十（列举用，加副词后缀 -ly）
什一税（同源旧词，指缴纳的十分之一）

senses.title: Coming after nine others
senses.definition: position number ten in a series
senses.definitionCN: 序列中的第十位
senses.example: Their office is on the tenth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的办公室在第十层。
senses.why: The ordinal marks the last finger in a full count, the edge of one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 序数标记整手点数后的最后一根手指，位于一双手的边缘。

senses.title: One part of ten equal parts
senses.definition: one of ten equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体十等分后的一份
senses.example: Rent takes a tenth of his salary.
senses.exampleCN: 房租占他工资的十分之一。
senses.why: A rank turns into a slice: the tenth item and the tenth share share one word.
senses.whyCN: 位次转成切片：第十项与第十份共享一词。

intro.en: Tenth is the ordinal of ten, formed in Old English with the Germanic -tha ending.
intro.cn: tenth 是 ten 的序数形式，古英语用日耳曼后缀 -tha 构成。

items.en: Old English teogotha was the ordinal of ten.
items.cn: 古英语 teogotha 是「第十」。

items.en: The -tha suffix built ordinals across the Germanic family, like German zehnte.
items.cn: -tha 后缀在日耳曼语族普遍构成序数，如德语 zehnte。

items.en: The deeper root dekm, ten, is a reconstructed Indo-European form.
items.cn: 更深的词根 dekm「十」是重构的印欧形式。

items.en: Spelling simplified to tenth, matching the hard th sound.
items.cn: 拼写简化为 tenth，与清辅音 th 一致。

items.en: The fraction sense grew with decimal mathematics.
items.cn: 小数数学的发展催生了「十分之一」义。

note.en: Tenth is set beside its cardinal and other ordinals.
note.cn: 把 tenth 与基数词及其他序数词并列。

entries.definition: the number itself
entries.definitionCN: 基数「十」

entries.definition: a cloth shelter; spelled without th, unrelated in sound use
entries.definitionCN: 帐篷；拼写相近，与序数无关

entries.definition: firmly fixed; looks similar in some fonts
entries.definitionCN: 紧的；字形略似但无关

entries.definition: the ordinal before tenth
entries.definitionCN: 第九

entries.definition: the ordinal after tenth
entries.definitionCN: 第十一

entries.definition: one of ten equal groups in statistics
entries.definitionCN: 十分位数（统计学术语）

normalIntro.en: Real links: ten plus th, the last finger, one slice of ten, and decile in statistics.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ten 加 th、最后一根手指、十等分之一、统计学的 decile。

normal.en: Tenth is ten wearing a th hat.
normal.cn: tenth 是戴着 th 帽子的 ten。

normal.en: The tenth floor is above nine floors.
normal.cn: 第十层在九层之上。

normal.en: A tenth of the pizza is one slice of ten.
normal.cn: 披萨的十分之一是十块中的一块。

normal.en: In tenth place: the last runner with a full count behind.
normal.cn: in tenth place：数满一双手后的最后一位。

normal.en: Decile is the Latin cousin of the tenth slice.
normal.cn: decile 是「十分之一」的拉丁表亲。

abstract.en: Ordinals are numbers wearing name tags.
abstract.cn: 序数是戴着名牌的数字。

abstract.en: The last finger closes the count and opens the fraction.
abstract.cn: 最后一根手指闭合计数，也开启分数。

abstract.en: Rank and share are one word apart.
abstract.cn: 位次与份额只隔一个词。

examples.en: She sits in the tenth row of the hall.
examples.cn: 她坐在大厅第十排。

examples.en: Only a tenth of applicants passed the test.
examples.cn: 只有十分之一的申请者通过了考试。

examples.en: The tenth of October is his birthday.
examples.cn: 十月十日是他的生日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「疼死」——跑第十名累得疼死 → tenth 第十

root: 古英语 teogotha「第十」，ten 的序数形式，日耳曼序数后缀 -tha 构成；与拉丁 decimus（第十）同出印欧 dekm。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses only: the rank after nine, and the slice of ten.
sensesIntro.cn: 仅两个义项：九之后的位次，与十等分之一。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last of ten counted fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：十根被数手指的最后一根。

branches.en: A name tag on position ten.
branches.cn: 挂在第十位上的名牌。

branches.en: The whole cut into ten identical slices.
branches.cn: 整体被切成十等份。

branches.en: Rank above, share below, one form.
branches.cn: 上是位次，下是份额，同一词形。

branches.en: Percentages and decimals live here.
branches.cn: 百分比与小数住在这里。

branches.en: Floors, rows and dates all borrow it.
branches.cn: 楼层、排次与日期都借用它。

intro.en: Tenth belongs to the Germanic ordinal family built with -th.
intro.cn: tenth 属日耳曼序数词族，以 -th 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordinals used -imus, as in decimus, tenth; English borrowed only the fraction idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语序数用 -imus 构成，如 decimus「第十」；英语只借入了「十分之一」的概念。

items.meaning: in the tenth place of a list

definition_zh: 学期；术语；条款；期限；措辞；把…称为
definition_en: a fixed period of time, a word with a special meaning, a condition of an agreement, or a school period
core_image: 一块立在时间线上的界石，也立在词典与合同里
scene: 新学期第一课，老师在黑板上写下这门课最难的术语。Students must learn the technical terms of biology.
sceneCN: 这里 term 是「术语」（第 2 个义项：专门领域的固定用语）；句意：学生必须学习生物学的专业术语。

collocations.phrase: under the terms of the contract

derivatives.zh: 末端的；终点站（同根形容词与名词）
术语体系（term 加 -logy 构成）
终止（同根动词）

senses.title: A fixed period of time
senses.definition: a set length of time, especially a school term or an office term
senses.definitionCN: 固定的时段，尤指学期或任期
senses.example: The autumn term begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季学期九月开始。
senses.why: The root is a boundary stone: a term is the space between two marks in time.
senses.whyCN: 词根是界石：term 就是时间线上两个界标之间的一段。

senses.title: A word with a special meaning
senses.definition: a word or expression with a precise meaning in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域具有精确含义的词或表达
senses.example: Photosynthesis is a basic term in botany.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用是植物学的基本术语。
senses.why: A boundary in language: the word marks exactly where one meaning stops and another begins.
senses.whyCN: 语言中的界石：这个词精确标出意义与意义之间的边界。

senses.title: A condition of an agreement
senses.definition: one of the conditions of a contract or agreement, usually plural
senses.definitionCN: 合同或协议的条件之一，多用复数
senses.example: They agreed to the terms of the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同意了租约条款。
senses.why: Terms are the boundary lines drawn inside an agreement: each clause ends a dispute before it starts.
senses.whyCN: 条款是协议内部的界线：每一条都在争执发生前划下终点。

senses.title: A way of expressing something
senses.definition: the particular words or style used to express something, in terms of or in plain terms
senses.definitionCN: 表达某事所用的话语或风格，用于 in terms of 等
senses.example: Explain the plan in simple terms.
senses.exampleCN: 用简单的措辞解释这个计划。
senses.why: Choosing terms is placing markers in speech: the same thing can be fenced with different words.
senses.whyCN: 选词就是在言语里立界标：同一件事可以用不同的词围出不同的说法。

senses.title: To give a name to
senses.definition: to describe or name something in a particular way, usually passive
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式称呼或描述，多用被动
senses.example: The project was termed a great success.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目被称为巨大成功。
senses.why: To term is to attach a fixed label, fixing the boundary of what a thing shall be called.
senses.whyCN: to term 就是贴上固定标签，划定某物名称的边界。

senses.title: The end of a pregnancy or of life
senses.definition: the end of a pregnancy carried full time, or the end of life, in full term or in terminally ill contexts
senses.definitionCN: 妊娠足月，或生命的末期，见于 full term 等
senses.example: The baby was born at full term.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿足月出生。
senses.why: The boundary sense returns literally: the end mark of gestation or of life.
senses.whyCN: 「界石」义字面回归：妊娠或生命终点的标记。

intro.en: Term comes from Latin terminus, the boundary stone, the same root as terminal and terminate.
intro.cn: term 源自拉丁语 terminus「界石」，与 terminal、terminate 同根。

items.en: Terminus named a boundary stone and its guardian god.
items.cn: terminus 既指界石，也是守护边界之神的名字。

items.en: The deeper origin of terminus is debated; links to words for stake or fixed mark are proposed but unproven.
items.cn: terminus 的更早来源有争议；与「木桩、固定标记」的联系有此一说但未确证。

items.en: Old French terme passed the word to English in two shapes of meaning: time-limit and expression.
items.cn: 古法语 terme 把「时限」与「用语」两义传给英语。

items.en: Medieval schools fixed the school-term sense and logic used term for a concept word.
items.cn: 中世纪学校确立了学期义，逻辑学用 term 指概念词。

items.en: Contracts, science and computing multiplied the word: terms of service, term paper.
items.cn: 契约、科学与计算使该词激增：服务条款、学期论文。

note.en: Term is compared with its boundary-word family and with words for periods and expressions.
note.cn: 把 term 与「界石」词族及表示时段、用语的词对比。

entries.definition: to end something

normalIntro.en: Real links: terminus the stone, the school calendar, contract clauses, and in terms of.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：界石 terminus、校历、合同条款、in terms of。

normal.en: Terminus marks where the field stops; term marks where time or meaning stops.
normal.cn: terminus 标记田地止步处；term 标记时间或意义的止步处。

normal.en: The autumn term is a fenced stretch of the year.
normal.cn: 秋季学期是被围起来的一段年历。

normal.en: Technical terms are words with fences around them.
normal.cn: 术语就是围了栅栏的词。

normal.en: Come to terms with it: draw the boundary and accept it.
normal.cn: come to terms with：划下界线并接受。

normal.en: In the long term: beyond the next boundary stone.
normal.cn: in the long term：越过下一块界石之后。

abstract.en: A term is a fence you agree to stand inside.
abstract.cn: term 是你同意站进去的一道栅栏。

abstract.en: Every definition begins by placing a stone.
abstract.cn: 每个定义都从立一块石头开始。

abstract.en: To name a thing is to end its vagueness.
abstract.cn: 为事物命名，就是终结它的模糊。

examples.en: The new term starts on the first Monday of September.
examples.cn: 新学期于九月第一个周一开学。

examples.en: Photosynthesis is a term every biology student learns.
examples.cn: 光合作用是每个生物学生都要学的术语。

examples.en: Read the terms before you sign the contract.
examples.cn: 签约前先读一遍条款。

sensesIntro.en: One stone, many fences: the calendar term, the contract term, the technical term.
sensesIntro.cn: 一块石头，多种栅栏：校历的学期、合同的条款、专业的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone planted in time and in language.
core.cn: 核心意象：插在时间与语言里的界石。

branches.en: The calendar is a row of stones.
branches.cn: 日历是一排界石。

branches.en: A term fences one meaning inside a field.
branches.cn: 术语把一个意义围在领域之内。

branches.en: Clauses are fences agreed by two hands.
branches.cn: 条款是两只手共同竖起的栅栏。

branches.en: To speak is to place stones in the air.
branches.cn: 说话就是在空中立石。

branches.en: The body also keeps its own calendar.
branches.cn: 身体也保有自己的历法。

intro.cn: term 与 terminal、terminate、terminology 同属 terminus 词族。

latinIntro.cn: 词基为拉丁语 terminus「界石」；其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: a period; a word; a condition

definition_zh: 末端的；终点的；晚期的；航站楼；终端机；终点站
definition_en: at the end of something; relating to a fatal illness; also a building or device at the end of a line
core_image: 线路尽头那扇亮灯的门
scene: 机场大厅尽头，玻璃幕墙外停着最后一班摆渡车。Passengers waited quietly in Terminal Two.
sceneCN: 这里 terminal 是名词「航站楼」（第 4 个义项：线路或交通的终点设施）；句意：旅客在二号航站楼安静等候。

derivatives.zh: 晚期地；末端地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
终止；结束（同根动词，-ate 为动词后缀）

senses.title: At the end of something
senses.definition: placed or happening at the end of a line, journey, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于线、旅程或结构的末端
senses.example: The train stopped at the terminal station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车停在终点站。
senses.why: The root means boundary: whatever is terminal touches the final mark.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「界标」：凡 terminal 之物都触到了最后的界线。

senses.title: Of an illness that ends in death
senses.definition: describing an illness that cannot be cured and will cause death
senses.definitionCN: 形容无法治愈、将致死亡的疾病
senses.example: The doctor told him the illness was terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诉他病已到晚期。
senses.why: Life itself reaches its boundary; the end mark falls on the body.
senses.whyCN: 生命本身抵达界线：终点标记落在了身体上。

senses.title: A point where a line ends or meets
senses.definition: a point where wires or systems connect or end
senses.definitionCN: 线路连接或终止之点
senses.example: Check the battery terminals before starting.
senses.exampleCN: 启动前检查电池接线端。
senses.why: A boundary is also a contact point: where a line stops, another may begin.
senses.whyCN: 界线也是接触点：一条线停驻之处，另一条线可以开始。

senses.title: A building for passengers or goods at the end of a route
senses.definition: a building at an airport, port, or bus station where journeys end or start
senses.definitionCN: 机场、港口或车站里旅程开始或结束的建筑
senses.example: The airport terminal opened at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 航站楼在黎明开放。
senses.why: The endpoint of a route grows walls and roofs; the boundary becomes a place.
senses.whyCN: 路线的端点长出墙与屋顶：界线变成了场所。

senses.title: A device for entering a computer system
senses.definition: a screen and keyboard connected to a main computer or network
senses.definitionCN: 连接主机或网络的屏幕与键盘设备
senses.example: She logged in at a library terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 她在图书馆的终端机上登录。
senses.why: The device sits at the edge of the network, where the user touches the system.
senses.whyCN: 设备位于网络边缘，正是用户触碰系统之处，故称终端。

senses.title: Final and not open to change
senses.definition: final, forming the end of a series or process
senses.definitionCN: 构成系列或过程之终点的
senses.example: The court made a terminal ruling in the case.
senses.exampleCN: 法院就本案作出终局裁定。
senses.why: Once the boundary is crossed, nothing continues beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 界线一旦越过，其后便再无延续。

intro.en: Terminal comes from Latin terminalis, of a boundary, built on terminus, the boundary stone or end point.
intro.cn: terminal 源自拉丁语 terminalis「属于界标的」，词基 terminus 意为界石、端点。

items.en: Terminus was the god and the stone of boundaries in Roman fields.
items.cn: terminus 是罗马田界之神，也指界石。

items.en: Terminalis meant belonging to a boundary or end.
items.cn: terminalis 意为属于边界或端点的。

items.en: The deeper origin of terminus before Latin is uncertain; a link with words for stake or mark has been suggested.
items.cn: terminus 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定；有说法将其联系到「木桩、标记」。

items.en: English borrowed terminal in the fifteenth century for words ending a clause or a limb tip.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入 terminal，先指从句末词与肢体末端。

items.en: Railways gave the station sense, medicine the fatal sense, computing the device sense.
items.cn: 铁路带来终点站义，医学带来晚期义，计算带来终端机义。

note.en: Terminal is compared with its Latin family and with words of ending.
note.cn: 把 terminal 与拉丁词族及表示终结的词对比。

entries.definition: the Latin word for an end point, used for final stations

normalIntro.en: Real links: terminus the boundary stone, the airport hall, the battery contact, and terminal illness.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：界石 terminus、机场大厅、电池接点、晚期疾病。

normal.en: Terminus was a stone at the edge of the field: terminal is anything at the edge.
normal.cn: terminus 是田边的石头：terminal 就是任何位于边缘之物。

normal.en: Terminal Two: the end of the air route has a building.
normal.cn: 二号航站楼：航线终点长出了建筑。

normal.en: Battery terminals are where the current ends and begins.
normal.cn: 电池端点是电流的终点与起点。

normal.en: A computer terminal is the edge of the network.
normal.cn: 计算机终端是网络的边缘。

normal.en: Terminal illness: the life line reaches its last mark.
normal.cn: 晚期疾病：生命之线到达最后刻度。

abstract.en: Every line owns one point where it stops pretending.
abstract.cn: 每条线都拥有一个不再假装延伸的点。

abstract.en: A boundary is a door: it can end a journey or begin one.
abstract.cn: 边界是一扇门：可以终结旅程，也可以开启旅程。

abstract.en: Endings do not always mean death; sometimes they mean arrival.
abstract.cn: 终点未必意味着死亡；有时意味着抵达。

examples.en: The ferry terminal was crowded with summer travellers.
examples.cn: 渡轮码头挤满了夏季旅客。

examples.en: New treatment gave hope even to patients with terminal illness.
examples.cn: 新疗法甚至给晚期患者带来希望。

examples.en: Loose terminals made the radio fail.
examples.cn: 接线端松动导致收音机失灵。

sensesIntro.en: From boundary stone to edge marks everywhere: stations, diseases, wires, screens.
sensesIntro.cn: 从界石出发，长出各处的边缘标记：车站、疾病、电线与屏幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone marking where the road stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：标记道路止步之处的一块石头。

branches.en: Routes end in buildings that hold the boundary.
branches.cn: 路线终结于承载边界的建筑。

branches.en: The body reaches its own boundary stone.
branches.cn: 身体抵达自己的界石。

branches.en: Where a line ends, contact begins.
branches.cn: 线止之处，接触开始。

branches.en: The user sits at the network's edge.
branches.cn: 用户坐在网络边缘。

branches.en: A ruling that closes the file for good.
branches.cn: 一笔永久归档的终局裁定。

intro.cn: terminal 是 terminus「边界」词族之首。

latinIntro.en: Latin terminus, boundary stone, gave terminalis and the whole family of end words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terminus「界石」生出 terminalis 与整个「终点」词族。

items.meaning: to drive beyond the boundary; destroy

definition_zh: 可怕的；骇人的；糟糕的；严重的
definition_en: causing fear or shock; or extremely bad in quality
core_image: 夜里关灯后墙上的影子突然张大嘴
scene: 山路拐弯处，司机看见对面车灯猛地扑来。The crash was a terrible sight.
sceneCN: 这里 terrible 是「骇人的」（第 1 个义项：令人恐惧的）；句意：车祸现场骇人。

derivatives.zh: 非常；可怕地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
使恐惧（同根动词）
恐怖（同根名词）

senses.title: Causing fear or horror
senses.definition: making people very frightened
senses.definitionCN: 使人极度恐惧的
senses.example: The storm made a terrible noise on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨在屋顶上发出骇人的声响。
senses.why: The root terrere means to frighten: this is the fright itself in adjective form.
senses.whyCN: 词根 terrere 意为吓人：此义就是恐惧本身的形容词形态。

senses.title: Very bad in quality
senses.definition: of very poor quality or standard
senses.definitionCN: 质量或水准极差的
senses.example: The food at that hotel is terrible.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆的饭菜糟透了。
senses.why: Shock at badness borrows the fright word: what is awful is treated as what scares.
senses.whyCN: 对「差」的震惊借用了恐惧词：糟到令人「害怕」的程度。

senses.title: Very great in degree
senses.definition: extreme in amount or force
senses.definitionCN: 程度或力度极大的
senses.example: The wall felt a terrible pressure in the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水对墙体形成巨大压力。
senses.why: Fear once measured size: the terrible force is one that dwarfs the person facing it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧曾被用来度量大小：可怕之力就是令人自感渺小之力。

senses.title: Feeling unwell or upset
senses.definition: feeling very ill or unhappy, as in feel terrible
senses.definitionCN: 感到极不舒服或难过，用于 feel terrible
senses.example: She felt terrible after the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后她难受极了。
senses.why: The inner state is described with the outer shock word: the body is under attack by feeling.
senses.whyCN: 用外在的震惊词形容内在状态：身体仿佛被情绪袭击。

intro.en: Terrible comes from Latin terribilis, to be feared, built on terrere, to frighten.
intro.cn: terrible 源自拉丁语 terribilis「令人畏惧的」，词基为 terrere「使恐惧」。

items.en: Terrere meant to frighten away or alarm.
items.cn: terrere 意为吓退、惊骇。

items.en: Terribilis described a thing that deserves fear.
items.cn: terribilis 形容值得畏惧之物。

items.en: Old French terrible fixed the spelling and the strong sense.
items.cn: 古法语 terrible 固定了拼写与强义。

items.en: English used terrible of God, war and punishment before everyday badness.
items.cn: 英语先用 terrible 形容神、战争与刑罚，后才用于日常的「差」。

items.en: Everyday use weakened the fear to simple badness or intensity.
items.cn: 日常用法把恐惧弱化为单纯的「差」或程度。

note.en: Terrible is compared with its fear family and with words for very bad things.
note.cn: 把 terrible 与恐惧词族及表示极差的词对比。

entries.definition: the adverb meaning very or frighteningly
entries.definitionCN: 副词：非常；可怕地

entries.definition: once frightening, now excellent
entries.definitionCN: 原为吓人的，今为极好的

entries.definition: intense fear
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖

entries.definition: very bad or unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 极坏的；令人不快的

entries.definition: extremely bad, with dread in the root
entries.definitionCN: 糟糕透顶的（词根含恐惧）

entries.definition: shocking or very bad
entries.definitionCN: 骇人的；极糟的

normalIntro.en: Real links: terrere to frighten, the terror family, and the everyday terrible weather.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：terrere「吓人」、terror 词族、日常的 terrible weather。

normal.en: Terrere means to frighten: terrible things make you gasp.
normal.cn: terrere 意为吓人：terrible 之事令人倒吸冷气。

normal.en: Terrific flipped its fear into praise.
normal.cn: terrific 把恐惧翻转成了称赞。

normal.en: Terrible weather is bad enough to scare a picnic.
normal.cn: terrible weather 糟到能吓跑野餐。

normal.en: Feel terrible: the shock turned inward.
normal.cn: feel terrible：震惊转向了体内。

normal.en: Terror is the noun, terrible the adjective, terribly the degree.
normal.cn: terror 是名词，terrible 是形容词，terribly 是程度。

abstract.en: Badness is measured in gasps.
abstract.cn: 「差」是用倒吸的冷气来计量的。

abstract.en: Some words age from terror into complaint.
abstract.cn: 有些词从恐怖老成了抱怨。

abstract.en: Fear once drew the map of size and strength.
abstract.cn: 恐惧曾描画大小与强弱的地图。

examples.en: The earthquake was terrible in both size and loss.
examples.cn: 这次地震无论规模还是损失都极为可怕。

examples.en: He made a terrible first impression at the interview.
examples.cn: 他在面试上留下了糟糕的第一印象。

examples.en: She felt terrible about forgetting the meeting.
examples.cn: 她为忘了会议而难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太惹怖」——太惹人怖了 → terrible 可怕的、糟糕的

root: 拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」→ terribilis「令人畏惧的」→ 古法语 terrible → 英语 terrible；terrify、terror 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From holy fear to everyday complaint: one adjective covers shock, badness and degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对神的敬畏到日常抱怨：一个形容词覆盖震惊、差劲与程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gasp at something too big or too bad.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对过大或过糟之物的一声惊呼。

branches.en: The fright itself.
branches.cn: 恐惧本身。

branches.en: Badness big enough to scare.
branches.cn: 大到吓人的差劲。

branches.en: Size expressed through fear.
branches.cn: 用恐惧表达的规模。

branches.en: The gasp turned inward.
branches.cn: 惊呼转向内心。

branches.en: The scale slides from horror to complaint.
branches.cn: 尺度从惊骇滑向抱怨。

intro.en: Terrible belongs to the terrere fear family shared with terrify and terror.
intro.cn: terrible 属 terrere「恐惧」词族，与 terrify、terror 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin terrere, to frighten, gave terribilis, terror and the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」产生 terribilis、terror 及英语词族。

definition_zh: 非常；极度；可怕地；糟糕地
definition_en: very or extremely; also in a frightening or bad way
core_image: 吓得两腿发软地——或只是「特别特别地」
scene: 孩子看完恐怖片，抱着枕头不敢关灯。The movie frightened him terribly.
sceneCN: 这里 terribly 是「可怕地」（第 1 个义项：令人恐惧地）；句意：电影把他吓得要命。

derivatives.zh: 可怕的；糟糕的（副词的形容词形式）
使恐惧（同根动词，-ify 为动词后缀）
恐怖（同根名词，terrere 加 -or）

senses.title: In a frightening way
senses.definition: in a way that frightens or shocks
senses.definitionCN: 以令人恐惧或震惊的方式
senses.example: The engine failed terribly in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 引擎在暴风雨中可怕地失灵了。
senses.why: The root is terror: the adverb keeps the fright image first.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 terror：副词首先保留「恐惧」画面。

senses.title: Very; extremely
senses.definition: to a very great degree, used before adjectives and verbs
senses.definitionCN: 程度极高，用于形容词与动词之前
senses.example: I am terribly sorry for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 对延误我万分抱歉。
senses.why: Intensity bleaches the fright: what shocks becomes simply what is extreme.
senses.whyCN: 强烈程度漂白了恐惧：令人震惊的变成单纯「极大的」。

senses.title: In a very bad way; badly
senses.definition: very badly or poorly
senses.definitionCN: 非常差地
senses.example: The team played terribly in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 球队上半场踢得很糟。
senses.why: The bad-quality sense stays close to the root: awful things are done awfully.
senses.whyCN: 「差」义紧贴词根：可怕之事做得可怕，即为糟糕。

intro.en: Terribly is the adverb of terrible, from Latin terrere, to frighten, through terribilis and Old French.
intro.cn: terribly 是 terrible 的副词，源自拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」，经 terribilis 与古法语传入。

items.en: Terrere meant to frighten or alarm.
items.cn: terrere 意为使恐惧、惊骇。

items.en: Terribilis meant frightful, to be feared.
items.cn: terribilis 意为可怕的、令人畏惧的。

items.en: Old French terrible carried the word into English spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 terrible 确立了英语拼写。

items.en: English added the native -ly to form the adverb.
items.cn: 英语加本族 -ly 构成副词。

items.en: Everyday speech bleached the fright into plain intensity: terribly good.

normalIntro.en: Real links: terrere to frighten, the terrible family, and the polite terribly sorry.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：terrere「使恐惧」、terrible 词族、礼貌用语 terribly sorry。

normal.en: Terrere means to frighten; terribly first meant frighteningly.
normal.cn: terrere 意为吓人；terribly 最初意为「吓人地」。

normal.en: Terribly sorry is politeness wearing a fear mask.
normal.cn: terribly sorry 是戴着恐惧面具的客气话。

normal.en: Terrify, terror, terrible: one root, three voices of fear.
normal.cn: terrify、terror、terrible：同一词根的三种恐惧声调。

normal.en: Dreadfully and awfully followed the same path: fear into intensity.
normal.cn: dreadfully 与 awfully 走过同一条路：恐惧变成程度。

normal.en: Played terribly: the fright turned into plain badness.
normal.cn: played terribly：恐惧变成了纯粹的差劲。

abstract.en: English intensives are a museum of old fears.
abstract.cn: 英语的程度副词是一座旧恐惧博物馆。

abstract.en: The stronger the feeling, the faster the fright fades.
abstract.cn: 感情越常用，恐惧退色越快。

abstract.en: Saying terribly sorry, you fear the offence, not the monster.
abstract.cn: 说 terribly sorry 时，你怕的是冒犯，不是怪物。

examples.en: The children were terribly excited about the trip.
examples.cn: 孩子们对这次旅行兴奋极了。

examples.en: The storm damaged the crops terribly.

examples.en: He sings terribly but loves it.

definition_zh: 领土；地盘；（动物的）领域；领域；地区
definition_en: an area of land under a particular authority, or an area that an animal, person, or group treats as its own
core_image: 一只动物沿着灌木丛嗅出一圈界线，把这片地划成自己的
scene: 两只狼在河谷边缘留下气味标记，警告外来者不要进入这片领地。 Two wolves left scent marks along the edge of the valley, warning outsiders not to enter their territory.
sceneCN: 这里 territory 是「（动物的）领域、地盘」（第 2 个义项：动物防卫的空间）；句意：两只狼在河谷边缘留下气味标记，警告外来者不要进入这片领地。

pos.zh: 领土；属地；地区；领域；地盘（可数，复数为 territories）

derivatives.zh: 领土的；地盘的；区域性的

senses.title: Land under a state's authority
senses.definition: the land and waters under the legal authority of a state or government
senses.definitionCN: 处于国家或政府法律管辖之下的陆地与水域
senses.example: The treaty fixed the northern territory of the two nations.
senses.exampleCN: 条约确定了两国的北部领土。
senses.why: Latin territorium first meant the land around a town, from terra 'earth'. The political sense grew by extending that 'land belonging to a centre' to a whole state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 territorium 最初指“城镇周围的土地”，来自 terra「土地」。政治义是把“属于某一中心的土地”扩展到整个国家。

senses.title: An animal's defended area
senses.definition: the area an animal or group defends against intruders of the same or other species
senses.definitionCN: 动物或群体防御同种或其他物种入侵的空间
senses.example: The male warbler sings at dawn to advertise his territory.
senses.exampleCN: 雄莺在黎明鸣唱以宣告自己的领域。
senses.why: The political notion of bounded land is applied to behaviour: a bird treats a patch as if it were owned, and trespass is met with song or attack.
senses.whyCN: “有边界的土地”这一政治概念被用于行为：鸟把一块地当作己有，入侵者会遭到鸣唱警告或攻击。

senses.title: A field of knowledge or activity
senses.definition: a domain of study, expertise, or action that belongs to a group or discipline
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一群体或学科的研究、专长或行动范围
senses.example: Genetic editing lies in territory that older regulations never covered.
senses.exampleCN: 基因编辑属于旧法规从未覆盖的领域。
senses.why: The spatial metaphor shifts from soil to concepts: an area is 'held' by a discipline just as land is held by a state, so new work is either inside or outside that boundary.
senses.whyCN: 空间隐喻从土地转向概念：一个学科“持有”某个区域，就像国家持有土地，因此新研究要么在边界内，要么在边界外。

senses.title: Commercial or sales area
senses.definition: a region assigned to a salesperson, branch, or company as its exclusive market
senses.definitionCN: 分配给销售员、分支机构或公司的专属市场区域
senses.example: The firm split the coast into three sales territories.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把沿海地区分成三个销售区域。
senses.why: Modern business reuses the oldest structure: a centre assigns a bounded patch to an agent, and the boundary is protected against rival sellers.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业复用了最古老的结构：中心把一块有边界的区域分给代理人，并防御竞争对手进入。

senses.title: A region or district
senses.definition: a general region of land, especially one with a distinguishing feature or administration
senses.definitionCN: 具有某种特征或行政建制的广大地带
senses.example: Mountain territory covers most of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 山区地带占该省的大部分。
senses.why: The word often simply names land at a regional scale, without the strict legal or behavioural sense; the boundary is geographic rather than defended.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常只指区域尺度的土地，不带严格的法律或行为含义；边界是地理性的，而非被防卫的。

senses.title: A dependent possession
senses.definition: a land governed by another country but not fully integrated into it
senses.definitionCN: 由另一国治理但未完全并入该国的土地
senses.example: The islands remain a territory of the mainland state.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿仍是大陆国家的属地。
senses.why: Imperial and colonial usage made territory the word for land held from outside; the people there may have rights of residence without full citizenship.
senses.whyCN: 帝国与殖民用法使 territory 成为“从外部持有的土地”的用词；当地居民可能拥有居住权而无法获得完整公民身份。

senses.title: Unfamiliar or dangerous ground
senses.definition: in figurative use, a situation or subject that people have not dealt with before
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻，指人们此前未曾应对过的处境或主题
senses.example: Negotiating with the rebels took the envoys into unknown territory.
senses.exampleCN: 与叛军谈判把使节带入了未知领域。
senses.why: The metaphor treats experience as a map: known land is charted, unknown land is territory without marks, and entering it means risk.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把经验当作地图：已知之地被测绘，未知之地是没有标记的 territory，进入它就意味着风险。

senses.title: A marked area in a game or sport
senses.titleCN: 比赛或运动中的场地范围
senses.definition: the part of a playing field or board assigned to a player or team
senses.definitionCN: 运动场或棋盘上分配给某一方或队员的区域
senses.example: The defender refused to leave his territory near the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫拒绝离开球门附近的防区。
senses.why: Games formalize the same instinct: space is divided and each player is responsible for one patch, so 'territory' becomes a rule rather than a claim.
senses.whyCN: 比赛把同一种本能形式化：空间被划分，每名球员负责一块区域，于是 territory 成为规则而不是主张。

intro.en: Territory came from Latin territorium, the land around a town. Its link to terra 'land' is clear, but a popular derivation from terrere 'to frighten' remains disputed, so that branch is marked uncertain.
intro.cn: territory 来自拉丁语 territorium，即城镇周围的土地。它与 terra「土地」的联系清楚，但流行的“来自 terrere「使恐惧」”一说仍有争议，故该分支标注为不确定。

items.en: English territory is recorded in the late fourteenth century meaning 'land under the jurisdiction of a town or lord'.
items.cn: 英语 territory 于 14 世纪晚期被记录，义为“城镇或领主管辖下的土地”。

items.en: From Latin territorium 'land around a town, domain, district'. The suffix -orium marks a place associated with something.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 territorium「城镇周围的土地、领地、区域」。后缀 -orium 标记与某物相关的地点。

items.en: The base is terra 'earth, land', which also gives terrain, terrace, Mediterranean and terracotta. This part of the history is well supported.
items.cn: 词基是 terra「土地」，还衍生 terrain、terrace、Mediterranean、terracotta。这部分历史有充分支持。

items.en: Some sources connect territorium with terrere 'to frighten' and territare 'to frighten repeatedly', which would make the original sense 'land kept by fear'. Standard references disagree, so this link is source uncertain.
items.cn: 有些资料把 territorium 与 terrere「使恐惧」、territare「反复恐吓」联系起来，那样原义会是“靠恐惧守住的土地”。通行资料并不一致，故该联系来源不确定。

items.en: The sense widened to colonial possessions and to figurative 'field of knowledge'; in the 20th century ethology borrowed it for defended animal space.
items.cn: 词义扩展到殖民地属地与比喻性的“知识领域”；20 世纪动物行为学又借它指被防卫的动物空间。

items.en: Modern English keeps the political, behavioural, commercial, and figurative senses side by side; the plural territories is standard.
items.cn: 现代英语并列保留政治、行为、商业与比喻义；复数 territories 为标准形式。

note.en: The first group separates form neighbours, the second compares words for land and defended space.
note.cn: 第一组区分词形相近者，第二组比较表示土地与防卫空间的词。

entries.definition: the physical surface of land, its slope and texture. It is ground as landscape, not ground as jurisdiction.
entries.definitionCN: 土地的地表形态、坡度与质地。它是作为景观的地面，而非作为管辖范围的地面。

entries.definition: a flat raised strip of land; from terra through French. It shares the earth base but not the political sense.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的台地；经法语来自 terra。共享“土地”词基，但无政治义。

entries.definition: extreme fear, from terrere 'to frighten'. It is not a relative unless the disputed territory link is accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 极度恐惧，来自 terrere「使恐惧」。除非接受有争议的 territory 联系，否则并非同源。

entries.definition: relating to territory; also the adjective for defensive behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 与领土有关的；也指防卫行为的形容词。

entries.definition: an area owned or controlled, often legal or feudal; also a field of expertise. It is more formal than territory.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有或控制的区域，常为法律或封建语境；也指专长领域。比 territory 更正式。

entries.definition: a broad area defined by geography or administration. It lacks the sense of defence or ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 由地理或行政界定的大片区域。缺少防卫或占有之义。

entries.definition: the area in which a species occurs. It is not necessarily defended.
entries.definitionCN: 物种出现的区域。不一定被防卫。

entries.definition: the surface or an area underfoot, or a field of argument. It is neutral and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 脚下的地面或场地，也指论点领域。中性且偏物理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, standard phrases, and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语成分、标准搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: terra means earth: territory is land marked off as belonging to someone.
normal.cn: terra 意为土地：territory 是被划出来、属于某人的土地。

normal.en: Mark its territory is the fixed phrase for animals leaving scent, sound, or visible signs.
normal.cn: mark its territory 是动物留下气味、声音或可见标记的固定说法。

normal.en: Terrain is the same land seen as surface; territory is the same land seen as ownership.
normal.cn: terrain 是把同一片土地看作地表；territory 是把同一片土地看作所有权。

normal.en: Sales territory shows how ordinary the structure is: a company assigns a patch to a seller.
normal.cn: sales territory 说明这个结构多么日常：公司把一块区域分给销售员。

normal.en: Unknown territory is the figurative branch: experience drawn as a map with blank areas.
normal.cn: unknown territory 是比喻分支：把经验画成一张留有空白的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in grass: on one side is 'mine', on the other 'not mine'. Territory is the area inside the line, however the line is made.
abstract.cn: 想象在草地上画一条线：一边是“我的”，另一边是“不是我的”。territory 就是线内的区域，无论线是怎么画出来的。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from states to animals to disciplines to sales because all four involve a centre assigning and defending a bounded area.
abstract.cn: 这个词能轻易从国家转到动物、学科、销售，因为四者都涉及一个中心分配并防卫有边界的区域。

abstract.en: Behavioral territory is not property in law; it is a claim enforced by presence, not by title.
abstract.cn: 行为学上的领域不是法律财产；它是由在场维系的 claim，而不是由产权证维系。

examples.en: The river forms the eastern boundary of the territory.
examples.cn: 这条河构成该领土的东部边界。

examples.en: Robins defend their territory against intruders throughout the spring.
examples.cn: 整个春天，知更鸟都在防御领地、抵御入侵者。

examples.en: The question of consciousness is still unexplored territory for the lab.
examples.cn: 意识问题对该实验室仍是未探索的领域。

dict_mnemonic.text: “太弱的里”——这片地里太弱的人守不住，只能让强敌占去 → territory 领地、领土

root: 拉丁语 territorium「城镇周围的土地」，词基 terra「土地」；与 terrere「使恐惧」的联系存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of territory: a bounded area held by a state, an animal, a discipline, a company, a game, or the imagination. The common core is 'land marked as belonging'.
sensesIntro.cn: territory 的八个义项：由国家、动物、学科、公司、比赛或想象持有的有边界区域。共同核心是“被标记为属于某方的土地”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn around a patch of ground, with 'mine' inside and 'not mine' outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一片土地周围画一条线，线内是“我的”，线外是“不是我的”。

branches.en: POLITICS: land under a state, including dependent possessions beyond the core.
branches.cn: 政治：国家管辖的土地，包括核心之外的属地。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR AND PLAY: animals and players defend an assigned patch.
branches.cn: 行为与比赛：动物与球员防卫被分配的区域。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: a discipline's field, or the blank part of the map called unknown.
branches.cn: 知识：学科领域，或被称作“未知”的地图空白部分。

branches.en: COMMERCE: a company assigns a market patch to an agent.
branches.cn: 商业：公司把一块市场区域分给代理人。

branches.en: GEOGRAPHY: a broad region named by its features rather than by defence.
branches.cn: 地理：以特征而非防卫命名的广大地区。

intro.en: Territory is a Latin noun in -orium, a suffix of place. English adds the adjective and noun suffixes -ial and -iality, but does not build the root anew.
intro.cn: territory 是带 -orium（地点后缀）的拉丁名词。英语只加形容词与名词后缀 -ial、-iality，并不重新构造词根。

latinIntro.en: Terra 'earth' yields terrain, terrace, terracotta, and Mediterranean; the territorium branch yields territorial, territoriality, and the verb territorialize.
latinIntro.cn: terra「土地」衍生 terrain、terrace、terracotta、Mediterranean；territorium 这一支衍生 territorial、territoriality 与动词 territorialize。
